This article reproduces, with every call visible, the regional-consistency strategy of the
mrct-consistency technical report: a multiregional trial is positive overall, one region looks
unfavourable, and a subgroup identified by `forestsearch()` **on the patients outside the region** is
applied inside it.
The simulation design that generated the case study, and the campaign's results, are in the
companion article [mrct-consistency-simulations](mrct-consistency-simulations.html).

::: {.callout-note}
## Installing forestsearch

The CRAN release of forestsearch (0.4.0) does not yet contain the functions this article uses, so the
last step below installs the development version from GitHub. Run the steps in a fresh R session.

```r
# 1. a reliable CRAN mirror, and a longer download limit than R's default of 60 seconds
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"), timeout = 600)

# 2. the CRAN release, which installs every package forestsearch needs
install.packages("forestsearch")

# 3. two packages forestsearch only suggests, which this article uses (speff2trial for the
#    ACTG 175 data, latentcor for the copula expansion), knitr for the tables, and remotes for the next step
install.packages(c("speff2trial", "latentcor", "knitr", "remotes"))

# 4. the development version from GitHub; upgrade = "never" leaves the packages above as they are
remotes::install_github("larry-leon/forestsearch", upgrade = "never")
packageVersion("forestsearch")
```

Step 4 downloads the whole forestsearch repository, several gigabytes, and builds only the package
from it, so it takes several minutes; the longer download limit of step 1 is what lets it finish. If a
step asks whether to install packages from sources, answer no. The chunk below stops with a message
naming anything that is missing, before any computation starts.
:::

```{r install-check}

            "mr_estimates_table", "mrct_record", "fs_in_subgroup", "mrct_four_sets", "mrct_trial_analysis",
            "mr_values")
missing_fns <- setdiff(needed, getNamespaceExports("forestsearch"))
if (length(missing_fns))
  stop("This article needs the development version of forestsearch (see 'Installing forestsearch'); ",
       "the installed version (", as.character(packageVersion("forestsearch")), ") lacks: ",
       paste(missing_fns, collapse = ", "), ".", call. = FALSE)

if (length(missing_pkgs))
  stop("This article needs: ", paste(missing_pkgs, collapse = ", "),
       " (install.packages(c(", paste0('"', missing_pkgs, '"', collapse = ", "), ")).", call. = FALSE)
c(forestsearch = as.character(packageVersion("forestsearch")))
```

# Overview: the question and the design {#sec-overview}

## The trigger and the question

A global trial meets its primary endpoint: the upper 95% limit of the all-patient Cox hazard ratio is
below 1.0 (**ITT ub < 1.0**). The region of interest, about a fifth of the patients in our illustrations, has a Cox point estimate above 1.0 (**region ITT > 1.0**). This pair is the **trigger**: the regional
consistency failure as it presents in oncology multiregional clinical trials (MRCTs). 

The question is whether a subgroup identified based on the non-region patients can account for the regional result: if removing it from the region leaves a Cox estimate below 1.0, the regional result is suggestive/compatible with a trial-wide subgroup. We therefore cast the MRCT regional consistency criteria in terms of the identified subgroup -- whether the regional subgroup point estimate is below 1.0 -- as if the subgroup was pre-specified.  While the subgroup is not pre-specified, our proposal pre-specifies the identification procedure and does not include the regional data to which it is applied. The strategy is **signal generation, not confirmation**.

We consider two mechanisms for the trigger:

- **a trial-wide harmed subgroup** — the explanation this article's analysis pursues: a subgroup effect present 
in the region and non-region populations, resulting in attenuation of the region's estimate (the region's prognostic effect and the finite follow-up window shaping how far);
- **a region-specific effect** — the region differs in its treatment effect. The analysis approach
  does not pursue this explanation; it enters through the extension of @sec-dgm-overview, whose
  configurations with no regional treatment benefit (the true region effect is $> 1.0$) quantify how often the strategy
  falsely leads to meeting consistency in an identified subgroup — the false-positive rate of the
  subgroup pathway.  


::: {.callout-important}
## The region in this article
ACTG 175 was not a multiregional trial and has no region variable. We are utilizing this dataset because 
it is publicly available and the trial collected survival and GLM (binary and continuous) outcomes. The region used here is
hypothetical: about 20% of patients, planted in a simulated population by a logistic model
(the simulations article). The way a region enters an analysis differs between real data and simulation:

- **In a real analysis** the region is an observed column of the trial data and nothing about it is
  modelled. The trial is split into the region's patients and the rest; the identifier runs on the
  rest; the declared rule is applied to the region.
- **In simulation** the region has to be generated together with the patients. Here, with no observed
  region, it is planted by a model. With a trial that has an observed region, the observed region is
  carried into the data-generating mechanism instead (the simulations article).

Replicate 5 of S2 (the simulation cell defined in @sec-dgm-overview), the case study, is one
simulated trial. From the point at which its data are read (@sec-case), it is analysed exactly as a
real trial would be.
:::

## The data-generating mechanism {#sec-dgm-overview}

Replicate 5 is one trial drawn from the report's S2 cell; we describe the mechanism behind it, stated
before the analysis so that its assumptions are clearly stated. Every simulated trial draws from a
Weibull accelerated-failure-time law built from ACTG 175 (the construction — the Weibull fit, the
copula expansion to a super-population of 20,000 rows, the planted region — is in the simulations article). For
patient $i$ on arm $z \in \{0, 1\}$, with baseline covariates $X_i$,
$$
\log T_i = \mu + \ell_z(X_i) + \tau\,\varepsilon_i, \qquad \varepsilon_i \sim \log \mathrm{Exp}(1),
$$
which is a proportional-hazards model with Weibull baseline: the hazard of patient $i$ on arm $z$ is
$\Lambda_0'(s)\, e^{\theta_z(X_i)}$ with $\Lambda_0(s) = (s\,e^{-\mu})^{1/\tau}$ and
$\theta_z(x) = -\ell_z(x)/\tau$. The log hazard splits into a prognostic part and a treatment part,
$$
\theta_z(X) = \theta_0(X) + z\,\psi(X), \qquad \theta_0(X) = X^\top \beta + r\,\mathbf 1\{X \in R\}.
$$
The regional prognostic effect enters only through $r$: an additive log-hazard shift carried by every
patient of the region, on both arms equally, leaving every patient's treatment effect untouched. The
planted subgroup $H^*$ carries the treatment-effect heterogeneity: the patient-level log hazard ratio
is
$$
\psi(X) = \log b + \log(h/b)\,\mathbf 1\{X \in H^*\},
$$
so the hazard ratio of treatment is $b$ outside $H^*$ and $h$ inside it, on both sides of the region
boundary. Here $H^* = \{\text{CD4} \le 230\}$.

The mechanism therefore assumes, inside and outside the region alike:

- **(M1) Proportional hazards within each patient**, with patient-specific ratio $e^{\psi(X)}$.
- **(M2) A common effect law across the region boundary** — $\psi$ does not involve $R$, so $(b, h)$
  are the same inside and outside the region. The extension below relaxes this: with
  treatment-by-region interactions $\gamma_R$ and $\gamma_{H^*\!R}$, $\psi$ may depend on $R$, the
  effects inside the region become $(b_R, h_R)$, and (M2) is then $\gamma_R = \gamma_{H^*\!R} = 0$.
- **(M3) A purely prognostic region** — $r$ shifts $\theta_0$ for all region patients and neither
  arm is favored.
- **(M4) Free regional composition** — the distribution of $X$, and with it the region's $H^*$
  share, may differ between the region and the non-region population per the observed configuration of ACTG 175 (we take patient's observed covariates as-is).

Under (M1)–(M4) any divergence of the region's windowed Cox limit from the trial's is produced by
composition and by the finite analysis window, not by any region-dependent treatment effect.

::: {.callout-note}
## The windowed Cox limit

A two-sample Cox fit of treatment on a set of patients — all patients, the region, or the region
minus a subgroup — assumes one hazard ratio for the set. With S2's design (entry uniform over 11
months, analysis at 40 months, so every patient is followed for 29 to 40 months), the estimate
converges, as the trial grows, to a limit that depends on the set and on that window: the set's
**windowed Cox limit**, margHR(40). With no censoring the limit is margHR($\infty$).

Every patient's hazard ratio is constant, but a set's is not. Compared among the patients still
event-free, the two arms' mean hazards start in the ratio of the set's CDE (the ratio of the arms'
mean hazards when every patient is at risk) and then drift as patients have events: the high-risk
patients first, and in $H^*$ the experimental patients, with hazard ratio $h$, faster than their
controls. margHR(40) is in effect an average of this drifting ratio over the events that fall inside
the window, so it depends on how far through the drift the window reaches, and that depends on the
set's event rate: higher hazards take the set through the drift faster, so the same 40 months cover
more of it. Under (M1)–(M4) this has two consequences. The hazard multiplier of S2 (below) moves
every margHR(40) while leaving each patient's hazard ratio, and each set's AHR, CDE and
margHR($\infty$), unchanged. And a region whose prognostic shift $r$ lowers its hazards ($r < 0$, as
in S2) goes through the drift more slowly, so in S2 its margHR(40) stays nearer its CDE than the
trial's does. The [appendix](#sec-window) shows both for S2, with a figure.
:::

Writing the effect with treatment-by-region interactions extends (M2):
$$
\psi(X) = \log b + \log(h/b)\,\mathbf 1\{X \in H^*\}
          + \gamma_R\,\mathbf 1\{X \in R\}
          + \gamma_{H^*\!R}\,\mathbf 1\{X \in H^*\}\,\mathbf 1\{X \in R\},
$$
with $\gamma_R = \log(b_R/b)$ and $\gamma_{H^*\!R} = \log(h_R/h) - \log(b_R/b)$: the hazard ratio of
treatment is $b$ outside and $b_R$ inside the region for patients outside $H^*$, and $h$ outside and
$h_R$ inside the region for patients in $H^*$. The base model is the null
$\gamma_R = \gamma_{H^*\!R} = 0$. Every cell of this article is the base model.

In S2, the cell that produced replicate 5:

- **effects** — $b = 0.55$ outside $H^*$, $h = 2$ inside it;
- **region** — about 20% of patients, planted by a logistic model with odds ratio 3 on symptomatic
  status and no CD4 term, with prognostic shift $r = -\log 4$;
- **hazard scale** — every hazard multiplied by 3, by shifting the Weibull intercept: $\mu$, as
  fitted to ACTG 175, is replaced by $\mu - \tau\log 3$, so that $\Lambda_0(s) = (s\,e^{-\mu})^{1/\tau}$
  becomes $3\,\Lambda_0(s)$ on both arms while every $\theta_z(X)$ is unchanged (the call is
  `scale_dgm_hazard(dgm, m = 3)`; the [appendix](#sec-window) uses it). The reason is the event
  rate: the Weibull fit to ACTG 175 carries that trial's own, about a fifth of patients within the
  40-month window, and the multiplier raises the design to about 40%, nearer a modern trial's event
  rate. It rescales event frequency only: every patient's hazard ratio — and with it $b$, $h$, and
  each set's AHR and CDE — is exactly as set (the windowed Cox limits do move, as the note above
  explains);
- **the trial** — $n = 1{,}000$ patients, 1:1, entry uniform over 11 months, analysed at 40 months,
  with administrative censoring only.

The full build, the other cells
and the checks against the committed record are in the companion article [mrct-consistency-simulations](mrct-consistency-simulations.html).

## Analytic predictions before the analysis {#sec-predictions}

Before a single Cox model is fitted, the design's event probabilities can be computed with no
simulation. Three calls do it:

1. rebuild the mechanism **from `rep5_trial.csv`**, with its region taken as observed and S2's
   stated effects ($h = 2$ in $H^*$ = {CD4 $\le$ 230}, $b = 0.55$ outside), and with two quantities
   estimated from the trial rather than set: the region's prognostic shift $r$, and the hazard scale;
2. `ahr_population()` at the design's window;
3. `ahr_design()` at the trial size.

There is no `scale_dgm_hazard()` call here: replicate 5's outcomes were drawn with every hazard
already multiplied by 3, so the Weibull fit to them estimates the scaled intercept directly, and a
`scale_dgm_hazard(…, m = 3)` call would multiply every hazard by 3 a second time.


```{r pre-build}
#| code-fold: show
trial_pre <- mrct_record("rep5_trial.csv")
trial_pre <- trial_pre[, setdiff(names(trial_pre), c("id", "flag_harm"))]  # a real trial has neither
names(trial_pre) <- sub("^z_", "", names(trial_pre))                       # plain names; the build adds z_
w_pre <- character(0)
t_pre <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
dgm_pre <- withCallingHandlers(
  inject_mrct_structure(
    trial_pre,
    outcome_var = "y_sim", event_var = "event_sim", treatment_var = "treat_sim",
    continuous_vars = c("age", "wtkg", "karnof", "preanti", "cd40", "cd80"),
    factor_vars = c("hemo", "homo", "drugs", "race", "gender", "symptom"),
    x_pred = "cd40",
    spline_spec = list(knot = 300, zeta = 800, log_hrs = rep(log(0.55), 3)),   # b = 0.55 everywhere
    region = list(observed = "region"),                                       # region as recorded; r estimated
    x3 = list(vars = "cd40", cuts = list(cd40 = 230), loghr = log(2 / 0.55)), # h = 2 in H*
    n_super = 20000, expand = "copula", seed = 7L,
    continuous_vars_cens = c("age", "cd40"), factor_vars_cens = "symptom"),
  warning = function(cnd) { w_pre <<- c(w_pre, conditionMessage(cnd)); invokeRestart("muffleWarning") })
pop_pre <- ahr_population(dgm_pre, analysis_time = 40, max_entry = 11)
p_pre <- ahr_design(pop_pre, b = 0.55, h = 2, n = 1000)$prob
t_pre <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t_pre
r_pre <- dgm_pre$mrct$region$prognostic_loghr
c(region_prognostic_loghr = r_pre, generating_r = -log(4),
  build_warnings = length(w_pre), seconds = round(t_pre, 1))
```

Seven design probabilities follow from four of them, built from three events (the event notation is in the [appendix](#sec-event-notation)):

- $A$ = {ITT ub < 1.0} — the trial is positive (the manuscript's $\mathrm{ITT}^+$);
- $B$ = {region ITT > 1.0} — the region's point estimate is unfavourable (the manuscript's
  $\mathrm{R}^-$);
- $C^*$ = {region($G^*$) < 1.0} — removing $H^*$ exactly leaves the region's estimate below 1.0 (the
  manuscript's $\mathrm{R}(G^*)^+$).

The named rows:

- **consistency** = $A \setminus B$ — the standard pathway: the trial is positive and the region is
  not above 1.0;
- **non-consistency (the trigger)** = $A \cap B$ — the standard pathway fails, and the investigation
  begins;
- **oracle consistency (the oracle joint)** = $A \cap B \cap C^*$ — the subgroup pathway, in its
  oracle form: the trigger occurs and removing $H^*$ exactly leaves the region below 1.0;
- **row (7)** — the two routes together: consistency and oracle consistency are mutually exclusive
  (the region is above 1.0 in one and not the other), so their probabilities add.

```{r pre-table}
#| code-fold: show
pA <- p_pre[["p_itt_ub_lt1"]]; pB <- p_pre[["p_region_itt_gt1"]]
pAB <- p_pre[["p_trigger"]];   pABC <- p_pre[["p_trigger_and_Gstar_lt1"]]
rows_pre <- c(pA, pB, pA - pAB, pAB, pABC, pAB - pABC, (pA - pAB) + pABC)
# identities by construction
stopifnot(near(rows_pre[3] + rows_pre[4], rows_pre[1], 1e-12),
          near(rows_pre[5] + rows_pre[6], rows_pre[4], 1e-12),
          near(rows_pre[3] + rows_pre[5], rows_pre[7], 1e-12))
lab <- c("(1) P(ITT ub < 1.0): the trial is positive",
         "(2) P(region ITT > 1.0)",
         "(3) P(consistency): positive, region ITT ≤ 1.0",
         "(4) P(non-consistency): the trigger",
         "(5) P(oracle consistency): the oracle joint",
         "(6) P(oracle non-consistency)",
         "(7) P(consistency or oracle consistency)")
knitr::kable(data.frame(row = lab, `from rep5_trial` = f3(rows_pre), check.names = FALSE),
             row.names = FALSE, align = "lr",
             caption = "Analytic predictions under S2's assumptions, computed from rep5_trial. The campaign-observed counterparts of these rows are in @sec-case-campaign and in the simulations article.")
```

This build estimates the region's prognostic shift and the hazard scale from the trial: $\hat r$ = `r f3(r_pre)`
($e^{\hat r}$ = `r f3(exp(r_pre))`), against the generating $-\log 4$ = `r f3(-log(4))` of
@sec-dgm-overview, and its covariates are one trial of 1,000 re-expanded by the copula — so these
values carry the sampling of that one trial, and a build from the full construction (the simulations
article) gives slightly different ones. Any build warnings are the censoring model's fit and are
explained in the simulations article.

Consistency, non-consistency and oracle consistency are the names used in the accompanying
manuscript; this article's trigger is the non-consistency event and its oracle joint the oracle
consistency, as the rows state.

*With your trial:* the same three calls, with your columns and your stated $H^*$, $b$ and $h$ (the
simulations article walks through them); if P(non-consistency) is very small at your design, a
campaign will have few triggered trials to summarise.

## The pipeline, for one trial

1. Fit the all-patient Cox model of treatment. If ITT ub $\ge$ 1.0, stop: the trial is not positive.
2. Fit the region's Cox model. If region ITT $\le$ 1.0, stop: the trigger is not reached.
3. Run the identifier, `forestsearch()`, on the non-region patients. It declares a subgroup $\hat H$,
   a rule in at most two baseline covariates, or nothing.
4. Apply $\hat H$ inside the region; $\hat G$ = region minus $\hat H$. Fit the region's Cox model on
   $\hat G$.
5. Record whether region($\hat G$) < 1.0; the trigger together with region($\hat G$) < 1.0 is
   **joint**. Record, as the oracle, whether region($G^*$) < 1.0, with $G^*$ = region minus the true
   harmed subgroup $H^*$. In simulation, also record the sensitivity and specificity of $\hat H$
   against $H^*$ on both sides.

::: {.callout-tip}
## The pipeline in one call

@sec-case runs the five steps one at a time, each call visible. `mrct_trial_analysis()` runs the
same pipeline in one call — @sec-one-call shows it on the case study and checks it against the
step-by-step objects.
:::

$\hat H$ is learned on the non-region patients only and applied to the region, whose outcomes the
identifier never sees: the region is a held-out test set, and its Cox fits on the whole region and
on $\hat G$ are ordinary Wald fits on sets defined by a fixed rule. The hold-out removes the subgroup selection, the region's fits carry no bias from a search their outcomes never entered.
The pipeline itself fully runs only when the region's estimate is above 1.0, so everything after
step 2 is conditioned on an unfavourable regional draw. While the analysis is post-hoc, we propose 
a pre-specified identifier algorithm (with key elements set in order to provide as much pre-specification as possible).  

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| trigger | ITT ub < 1.0 and region ITT > 1.0, in the same trial |
| $H^*$ | the true harmed subgroup, here CD4 $\le$ 230 cells/mm³ |
| $\hat H$ | the subgroup the identifier declares on the non-region patients |
| $\hat G$, $G^*$ | region minus $\hat H$; region minus $H^*$ (the oracle) |
| $\hat H^c$ | the non-region complement of $\hat H$: non-region patients not in $\hat H$ (not $\hat G$) |
| joint | the trigger and region($\hat G$) < 1.0; with $G^*$ in place of $\hat G$, the oracle joint |
| consistency / non-consistency | a positive trial with region ITT $\le$ 1.0; the trigger |
| Sens / Spec | of $\hat H$ against $H^*$, on the non-region patients and in the region |
| AHR | average hazard ratio of a set: $\exp$ of its patients' mean log hazard ratio |
| CDE | controlled direct effect: the ratio of the set's mean hazards under the two arms |
| margHR(40), margHR($\infty$) | the marginal hazard ratio: the limit of the set's two-sample Cox estimate at the 40-month analysis, and with no censoring |

: Labels used throughout.

::: {.callout-tip}
## How to use this article

@sec-case is the analysis of one trial, replicate 5 of S2, read from a shipped dataset and taken from
the first Cox fit to the bounds on the declared subgroup. With your own trial, follow the same steps
with your data frame and your column names; nothing in that section depends on how the trial arose.
The companion article [mrct-consistency-simulations](mrct-consistency-simulations.html) shows how to set up simulations around your trial, and contains the report's own simulation design, which
generated replicate 5, and its results.
:::

# The case study: replicate 5 of S2 {#sec-case}

This section analyses one trial from its data to its bounds. The trial is replicate 5 of S2, shipped
as `rep5_trial.csv` (one row per patient; its provenance is in `PROVENANCE.md`), and nothing below
reads the simulation sections. The columns are the ones the analysis uses:

- `id` — the patient;
- `y_sim`, `event_sim` — the time in months, and the event indicator;
- `treat_sim` — the treatment (1 = experimental);
- `z_region` — the region indicator;
- `z_age` to `z_symptom` — the twelve baseline covariates the identifier is given, on their natural
  scales;
- `flag_harm` — membership of $H^*$. A real trial has no `flag_harm`; here it is used only for the
  region($G^*$) row of step 4 and in the simulations article.

```{r case-read}
#| code-fold: show
trial <- mrct_record("rep5_trial.csv")
covs <- c("z_age", "z_wtkg", "z_karnof", "z_preanti", "z_cd40", "z_cd80",
          "z_hemo", "z_homo", "z_drugs", "z_race", "z_gender", "z_symptom")
# the replicate's call seed, from the MR campaign's record of this trial
seed_rep5 <- mrct_record("mr_field_S2_rep5.csv")$seed
stopifnot(length(seed_rep5) == 1, !anyDuplicated(trial$id),
          all(c("id", "y_sim", "event_sim", "treat_sim", "z_region", covs, "flag_harm") %in% names(trial)))
c(patients = nrow(trial), experimental = sum(trial$treat_sim == 1), events = sum(trial$event_sim),
  region = sum(trial$z_region == 1), non_region = sum(trial$z_region == 0), call_seed = seed_rep5)
```

*With your trial:* read your data frame, and name its time, event, treatment (1 = experimental) and
region (1 = in the region) columns and the baseline covariates the identifier may use: they are the
arguments of `mrct_trial_analysis()`, the one-call form of the steps below, which closes this section.

## Step 1: the all-patient Cox fit

```{r case-itt}
#| code-fold: show
fit_itt <- summary(coxph(Surv(y_sim, event_sim) ~ treat_sim, data = trial))
itt_ub <- fit_itt$conf.int[1, "upper .95"]
c(ITT_HR = fit_itt$conf.int[1, "exp(coef)"], lower = fit_itt$conf.int[1, "lower .95"], ITT_ub = itt_ub)
stopifnot(itt_ub < 1)
```

The upper 95% limit is `r f3(itt_ub)`, below 1.0: the trial is positive.
*With your trial:* `mrct_trial_analysis()` fits this from your time, event and treatment columns; if
ITT ub $\ge$ 1.0 the pipeline stops here, at stage `not_positive`.

## Step 2: the region's Cox fit, and the trigger

```{r case-region}
#| code-fold: show
reg <- trial$z_region == 1
fit_reg <- summary(coxph(Surv(y_sim, event_sim) ~ treat_sim, data = trial[reg, ]))
hr_reg <- fit_reg$conf.int[1, "exp(coef)"]
trigger <- itt_ub < 1 && hr_reg > 1
c(region_HR = hr_reg, lower = fit_reg$conf.int[1, "lower .95"], upper = fit_reg$conf.int[1, "upper .95"],
  region_events = sum(trial$event_sim[reg]), trigger = trigger)
stopifnot(trigger)
```

The region's estimate is `r f3(hr_reg)` (95% CI `r f3(fit_reg$conf.int[1, "lower .95"])`,
`r f3(fit_reg$conf.int[1, "upper .95"])`), above 1.0, from `r sum(trial$event_sim[reg])` events: the
trigger. The interval is wide, and a point estimate above 1.0 is not evidence that treatment harms
the region's patients; it is the second half of the trigger, and what it triggers is an
investigation, not a conclusion.
*With your trial:* `mrct_trial_analysis()` fits this from your region column; if region ITT
$\le$ 1.0 the pipeline stops here, at stage `no_trigger`.

## Step 3: the identifier on the non-region patients, with post-selection inference {#sec-rep5-mr}

`forestsearch()` runs on the non-region patients, with the region's patients passed as the test set
(`df.test`) to which the declared rule is applied, with the campaign's arguments:

- **candidates** — cuts on the observed covariates, with deciles for CD4, weight and prior ART, and
  at most two factors per rule;
- **the screen** — a candidate is admitted when its full-data hazard ratio is at least 0.90
  (`hr.threshold`);
- **the consistency requirement** — the candidate must show a hazard ratio of at least 0.80 in both
  halves of a random split of the data, in at least 90% of the splits (`hr.consistency`,
  `pconsistency.threshold`);
- **admissibility** — the identifier's subgroup-size and per-arm event minimums, at their defaults
  here;
- **selection** — among the candidates that pass, the declared subgroup is the largest within an
  effect neighbourhood of 0.20 of the largest effect.

Multiplier resampling (MR,
`mr_inference = TRUE`) follows in the same call: 2,000 Poisson multiplier draws, the complement
de-biased and given its own field (`include_complement`, `field_complement`), the field method at its
default Monte Carlo sizes, the re-selections returned, and the replicate's call seed. The call is the
one `mrct_case_study()` makes (see the simulations article), written out; it runs under R's default generator.

```{r case-fs}
#| code-fold: show
stopifnot(RNGkind()[1] == "Mersenne-Twister")
t_mr <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
fs <- forestsearch(
  df.analysis = trial[!reg, ], df.test = trial[reg, ],
  outcome.name = "y_sim", event.name = "event_sim", treat.name = "treat_sim", id.name = "id",
  confounders.name = covs, conf_force = character(0),
  conf.cont_jcuts = list(z_cd40 = 10, z_wtkg = 10, z_preanti = 10),
  use_grf = FALSE, use_lasso = FALSE, maxk = 2,
  hr.threshold = 0.90, hr.consistency = 0.80, pconsistency.threshold = 0.90,
  sg_focus = "hrMaxSG", effect_neighborhood = 0.20,
  mr_inference = TRUE,
  mr_inference_args = list(ci_method = "field", include_complement = TRUE, field_complement = TRUE,
                           draws = 2000, multiplier = "poisson", return_reselection = TRUE,
                           seed = seed_rep5),
  parallel_args = list(plan = "sequential"),
  show_candidate_summary = FALSE, details = FALSE, plot.sg = FALSE, quiet = TRUE)
t_mr <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t_mr
mr <- fs$mr_inference
Hhat_def <- paste(fs$sg.harm, collapse = " & ")
stopifnot(!is.null(fs$sg.harm), mr$ci_method == "field", mr$settings$draws == 2000,
          mr$field$n_out_used == mr$field$R_out)
c(seconds = round(t_mr, 1), candidate_family = mr$n_family, n_Hhat = mr$n_selected,
  n_Hhat_complement = mr$complement$n)
Hhat_def
```

$\hat H$ is `` `r Hhat_def` `` (`!{…}` is the complement): CD4 $\le$
`r sub(".*z_cd40 <= ([0-9.]+).*", "\\1", Hhat_def)` and prior ART over
`r sub(".*z_preanti <= ([0-9.]+).*", "\\1", Hhat_def)` days. The call took `r round(t_mr)` seconds on
one thread. *With your trial:* `df.analysis` and `df.test` are your non-region and region rows; your
column names go in `outcome.name`, `event.name`, `treat.name` and `id.name`, your covariates in
`confounders.name`, and those of your continuous covariates to be cut at deciles in `conf.cont_jcuts`;
the other arguments are the identifier's settings used throughout this article, and `seed` is yours.

## Step 4: $\hat H$ applied to the region; the four sets

Each set is analysed by the unweighted two-sample Cox fit of treatment, with the Wald 95% interval.
$\hat H$ is read for every patient from the identifier's selected rule (`fs_in_subgroup()`), checked against
its classification of the analysis and test sets; $\hat G$ is the region minus $\hat H$. The
region($G^*$) row is here only because the trial is simulated (`flag_harm`).

```{r case-sets}
#| code-fold: show
in_Hhat <- fs_in_subgroup(fs, trial)
stopifnot(identical(in_Hhat, trial$id %in% c(fs$df.est$id[fs$df.est$treat.recommend == 0],
                                              fs$df.test$id[fs$df.test$treat.recommend == 0])))
cox_set <- function(d) {
  f <- summary(coxph(Surv(y_sim, event_sim) ~ treat_sim, data = d))
  ex <- d$treat_sim == 1
  data.frame(n = nrow(d), n_exp = sum(ex), n_ctl = sum(!ex),
             events_exp = sum(d$event_sim[ex]), events_ctl = sum(d$event_sim[!ex]),
             hr = f$conf.int[1, "exp(coef)"], lo = f$conf.int[1, "lower .95"], hi = f$conf.int[1, "upper .95"])
}
Hstar <- trial$flag_harm == 1                       # simulation only: H* is unknown in a real trial
set_idx <- list(itt_all = rep(TRUE, nrow(trial)), itt_region = reg,
                region_Gstar = reg & !Hstar, region_Ghat = reg & !in_Hhat)
four <- data.frame(set = names(set_idx), do.call(rbind, lapply(set_idx, function(i) cox_set(trial[i, ]))),
                   row.names = NULL)
stopifnot(near(four$hr[1:2], c(fit_itt$conf.int[1, "exp(coef)"], hr_reg), 1e-12))
set_label <- c(itt_all = "All patients, ITT", itt_region = "Region, ITT",
               region_Gstar = "Region minus H* (G*)", region_Ghat = "Region minus Ĥ (Ĝ)")
knitr::kable(data.frame(Set = set_label[four$set], n = four$n,
                        `experimental n / events` = sprintf("%d / %d", four$n_exp, four$events_exp),
                        `control n / events` = sprintf("%d / %d", four$n_ctl, four$events_ctl),
                        HR = f3(four$hr), `95% CI` = sprintf("%s, %s", f3(four$lo), f3(four$hi)),
                        check.names = FALSE),
             row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrrr", caption = "Replicate 5 of S2: the four sets.")
```

`mrct_four_sets()` takes the trial's columns and this membership of $\hat H$, and its `plot()` draws the
forest plot and the Kaplan–Meier panels, by the code `plot()` uses for an `mrct_case_study` object
(simulations article).

```{r fig-case-forest}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3.2
#| fig-cap: "Replicate 5 of S2: hazard ratio, experimental vs control, with 95% CI (log scale)."
sets4 <- mrct_four_sets(trial, "y_sim", "event_sim", "treat_sim", region.name = "z_region",
                        in_Hhat = in_Hhat, truth.name = "flag_harm")
plot(sets4, which = "forest")
```

```{r case-km}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-cap: "Replicate 5 of S2: Kaplan–Meier by arm in the four sets (experimental blue, control black; months)."
plot(sets4, which = "km", time_unit = "months", analysis_time = 40)
```

The trial is positive (ITT upper limit `r f3(four$hi[1])` < 1.0) and its region is above 1.0
(`r f3(four$hr[2])`, `r four$events_exp[2] + four$events_ctl[2]` events): the trigger. Applied in the
region, $\hat H$ removes `r sum(in_Hhat & reg)` patients, and region($\hat G$) is
`r f3(four$hr[four$set == "region_Ghat"])`, below 1.0: the trial is joint. Every interval is wide: the
regional sets have few events, so the move of the regional estimate from above 1 to below 1 is an
explanation consistent with a trial-wide harmed subgroup, not confirmation of it. *With your trial:*
`fs_in_subgroup()` applies your $\hat H$ to all your rows; without `truth.name`, `mrct_four_sets()` drops
the region($G^*$) row, as $H^*$ is unknown.

::: {.callout-warning}
## What the move below 1.0 shows, and what it does not

Removing $\hat H$ from the region and refitting the Cox model compares two different patient sets; it
does not decompose the regional hazard ratio. The region's estimate is not a weighted average of the
estimates in $\hat H$ and in $\hat G$: removing patients changes the risk sets, the events and the
censoring mixture, and each Cox estimate converges to the limit of its own set at the analysis time
([appendix](#sec-window)), which can differ from that set's AHR or CDE. A regional estimate that moves
from above 1.0 to below 1.0 is therefore compatible with a trial-wide subgroup accounting for the
regional result. It does not show that $\hat H$ caused it, does not validate $\hat H$ as a
clinically actionable subgroup, and, read with the null cells of the simulations article, can arise
when there is no harmed subgroup at all. Nor is the distance between region($\hat G$) and
region($G^*$) a measure of how well $\hat H$ recovered $H^*$: they are different patient sets, and
each estimate converges to its own set's limit (the simulations article sets $\hat H$ against $H^*$
directly).
:::

## Step 5: the Pareto frontier and the bounds

**The Pareto frontier**: the admitted candidates that no other candidate beats on both hazard ratio
and size, with half-sample (split) 95% intervals from `compute_frontier_cis()` (1,000 random halvings
per member) and the effect neighbourhood 0.20 shaded; $\hat H$ is the selected member.

```{r frontier}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7
ci_front <- compute_frontier_cis(fs, n_splits = 1000L, seed = seed_rep5)
pf <- fs$grp.consistency$out_sg$pareto_frontier
stopifnot(nrow(ci_front) == nrow(pf), sum(pf$N == mr$n_selected & abs(pf$hr - mr$naive$est) < 1e-6) == 1)
print(plot_pareto_frontier(fs, ci_table = ci_front, show_band = TRUE, effect_neighborhood = 0.20))
```

**The inference table**, by `mr_estimates_table()` from the `forestsearch()` result alone. Two sets
are bounded, both among the non-region patients: $\hat H$ (row *Qstnbl*) and $\hat H^c$, its
non-region complement (row *Recmnd*). $\hat H^c$ is not $\hat G$; the region's outcomes play no part.

```{r mr-table}
mr_tab <- mr_estimates_table(fs, est.scale = "hr", digits = 3)
mv <- attr(mr_tab, "mr_values")
cc <- mr$complement; fl <- mr$field
stopifnot(near(mv$naive_est, c(mr$naive$est, cc$naive$est), 1e-12),
          near(mv$field_bound, c(fl$lower_1s, fl$complement$upper_1s), 1e-12),
          near(mv$bonferroni_bound, c(fl$joint$bonf_lower_H, fl$joint$bonf_upper_Hc), 1e-12))
mr_tab
```

Read by location: the naive hazard ratio of $\hat H$ is `r f3(mr$naive$est)` and its de-biased value
`r f3(mr$debiased$est)`, but the field lower bound is `r f3(fl$lower_1s)`,
`r if (fl$lower_1s < 0.90) "below 0.90" else "above 0.90 but below 1.0"`: once the selection is
accounted for, the data do not rule out a modest benefit in $\hat H$ — and a lower bound does not
establish harm there either. The field upper bound for $\hat H^c$ is `r f3(fl$complement$upper_1s)`,
below 1.0: the non-region patients outside $\hat H$ benefit. The two bounds are one-sided statements
about two different sets, not an interval for the contrast between them, so together they do not
establish that the two effects are separated; the Bonferroni pair in the table is the joint
statement. $\hat H$ is re-selected on a share `r f3(mr$reselection$p_hat[[mr$selected_index]])` of
the draws. *With your trial:* nothing changes;
`compute_frontier_cis()` and `mr_estimates_table()` take your `forestsearch()` result.

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading the bounds

`mr_estimates_table()` needs only the `forestsearch()` result run with `mr_inference = TRUE`. Read the
field lower bound for $\hat H$ by its location against the hazard ratios that would matter clinically
in your setting: a lower bound well below 1.0 leaves benefit in $\hat H$ open; one near or above 0.90
says that, after accounting for the selection, little benefit remains there. Read the field upper
bound for $\hat H^c$ the same way: below 1.0 says the non-region patients outside $\hat H$ benefit.
Use the Bonferroni pair when both statements are made together. The naive estimate in $\hat H$ is
selected and is not a bound. The field bounds are not ordinary intervals computed after treating
$\hat H$ as fixed: they are selection-adjusted by construction, bounds over the multiplier draws of
the whole candidate family. The re-selection share $\hat p(\hat H)$ is a stability diagnostic for
the exact declared rule: a small share says another rule would often have been declared from similar
data. It does not say whether neighbouring rules or the broader patient pattern are stable, and it
is not evidence for or against a harmed subgroup existing.

These bounds are for sets among the non-region patients. The region's fits on the whole region and
on $\hat G$ are ordinary Wald fits on sets defined by a fixed rule, with the region's few events; read
their intervals by location as well.
:::

Because replicate 5 is simulated, its $\hat H$ can also be set against $H^*$ and its estimates against
their limits; that needs the simulation design, and is in the simulations article.

## The S2 campaign in brief {#sec-case-campaign}

Replicate 5 is one trial of S2. The campaign ran 10,000 trials of the same design (the simulations
article). The first table gives the campaign-observed counterparts of the analytic rows of
@sec-predictions — unconditional, over all trials; the second follows the pipeline of this section,
conditional on the trigger where its denominators say so. The numbers are read from the campaign's
records, shipped with the package.

```{r case-campaign}
cc_core <- mrct_record("core_full_numeric.csv")
cc_core <- cc_core[cc_core$setting == "S2_rmlog4", ]
cc_disp <- mrct_record("core_n1000.csv")
stopifnot(nrow(cc_core) == 1, cc_core$replicates == 10000)
# the trial-positive count, from the display record's first row for S2 ("...; N of M)")
r1 <- cc_disp$value[cc_disp$row == "r1" & cc_disp$column == "S2"]
n_A <- as.numeric(gsub(",", "", sub("^.*; ([0-9,]+) of [0-9,]+\\)$", "\\1", r1)))
reps <- cc_core$replicates
n_trig <- cc_core$n_trigger
n_orac <- cc_core$n_Gstar_lt1
n_dcl  <- cc_core$n_declared_Ghat_lt1
stopifnot(length(n_A) == 1, !is.na(n_A), n_trig <= n_A, n_orac <= n_trig, n_dcl <= n_trig)
# row (2), over all trials: the entry-cells record's S2 column is this campaign (three shared counts checked)
cc_ent <- mrct_record("entry_cells_core_numeric.csv")
cc_ev <- function(q) cc_ent$S2[cc_ent$quantity == q]
n_B <- round(cc_ev("p_region_itt_gt1") * reps)
stopifnot(cc_ev("n_trials") == reps, near(cc_ev("p_region_itt_gt1") * reps, n_B), n_trig <= n_B,
          near(c(cc_ev("p_itt_ub_lt1"), cc_ev("p_trigger"), cc_ev("p_trigger_Gstar_lt1")) * reps,
               c(n_A, n_trig, n_orac)))
counts <- c(n_A, n_A - n_trig, n_trig, n_orac, n_trig - n_orac,
            (n_A - n_trig) + n_orac, n_dcl, (n_A - n_trig) + n_dcl)
obs <- counts / reps
# identities by construction: (3)+(4)=(1), (5)+(6)=(4), (3)+(5)=(7), (3)+(8)=(9)
stopifnot(near(obs[2] + obs[3], obs[1], 1e-12), near(obs[4] + obs[5], obs[3], 1e-12),
          near(obs[2] + obs[4], obs[6], 1e-12), near(obs[2] + obs[7], obs[8], 1e-12))
lab_obs <- c("(1) P(ITT ub < 1.0): the trial is positive",
             "(3) P(consistency): positive, region ITT ≤ 1.0",
             "(4) P(non-consistency): the trigger",
             "(5) P(oracle consistency): the oracle joint",
             "(6) P(oracle non-consistency)",
             "(7) P(consistency or oracle consistency)",
             "(8) P̂(declared consistency)",
             "(9) P̂(consistency or declared consistency)")
knitr::kable(data.frame(row = append(lab_obs, "(2) P(region ITT > 1.0)", after = 1),
                        `campaign-observed` = append(sprintf("%s (%s)", f3(obs), big(counts)),
                                                     sprintf("%s (%s)", f3(n_B / reps), big(n_B)), after = 1),
                        check.names = FALSE),
             row.names = FALSE, align = "lr",
             caption = "S2 at n = 1,000, campaign-observed over 10,000 trials; rows as in @sec-predictions, identities asserted.")
```

```{r case-campaign-pipeline}
cc_mr <- mrct_record("mr_field_core.csv")
stopifnot(sum(cc_mr$row == "lb_100") == 1,
          sum(cc_ent$quantity %in% c("trigger_n", "joint", "Ghat_region")) == 3)
camp <- list(
  reps = reps, n_trig = n_trig, n_decl = cc_core$n_declared, n_joint = n_dcl,
  lb100 = as.numeric(cc_mr$S2[cc_mr$row == "lb_100"]),
  ghat_reg = cc_ev("Ghat_region"))
camp$p_trig <- 100 * camp$n_trig / camp$reps
camp$p_decl <- 100 * camp$n_decl / camp$n_trig
camp$p_joint <- 100 * camp$n_joint / camp$n_trig
# the two records agree on S2
stopifnot(camp$n_trig == cc_ev("trigger_n"), abs(camp$p_joint - cc_ev("joint")) <= 1e-9)
# the reading's verbal claims
stopifnot(round(camp$p_trig / 25) == 1, abs(camp$p_joint - 50) < 5)
pc1 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 1)
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    step = c("trigger: ITT ub < 1.0 and region ITT > 1.0", "subgroup declared",
             "Ĥ field lower bound (one-sided 95%) > 1.0", "declared, region(Ĝ) < 1.0",
             "Ĝ, % of region patients"),
    S2 = c(sprintf("%s (%s)", pc1(camp$p_trig), big(camp$n_trig)),
           sprintf("%s (%s)", formatC(camp$p_decl, format = "f", digits = 2), big(camp$n_decl)),
           pc1(camp$lb100),
           sprintf("%s (%s)", pc1(camp$p_joint), big(camp$n_joint)),
           pc1(camp$ghat_reg)),
    of = c(sprintf("all trials (%s)", big(camp$reps)), "triggered trials", "declared triggered trials",
           "triggered trials", "declared triggered trials")),
  align = "lrl",
  caption = "Conditional on the trigger: the pipeline of this section, as often as it went each way (each row's denominator stated).")
```

Read unconditionally: the trial is positive in `r f3(obs[1])` of trials; consistency holds outright
in `r f3(obs[2])`, and the trigger occurs in `r f3(obs[3])` — about one S2 trial in four. The oracle
resolution holds in `r f3(obs[4])` of all trials (row 5) and the declared subgroup's in
`r f3(obs[7])` (row 8), so the two routes together give `r f3(obs[6])` by the oracle pathway and
`r f3(obs[8])` by the declared pathway (rows 7 and 9). Conditional on the trigger: a subgroup was
declared in `r big(camp$n_decl)` of `r big(camp$n_trig)` triggered trials, region(Ĝ) was below 1.0
in about half (`r pc1(camp$p_joint)`%), and Ĝ kept on average `r pc1(camp$ghat_reg)`% of the
region's patients. The field lower bound for Ĥ was above 1.0 in `r pc1(camp$lb100)`% of the declared
triggered trials; in the others it lies below 1.0, and it is read by its location, as for replicate
5 in step 5. Replicate 5 is one of the triggered trials with region(Ĝ) < 1.0.

## The one-call form {#sec-one-call}

`mrct_trial_analysis()` is steps 1 to 5 in one call: the two Cox fits and the trigger, the identifier on
the non-region patients with multiplier resampling, $\hat H$ applied to every row, and the four sets. Here
it runs on the same trial, with the identifier's arguments of step 3 and the record's seed.

```{r one-call}
#| code-fold: show
one_call <- mrct_trial_analysis(
  trial, "y_sim", "event_sim", "treat_sim", region.name = "z_region", id.name = "id",
  truth.name = "flag_harm",
  fs_args = list(confounders.name = covs, conf_force = character(0),
                 conf.cont_jcuts = list(z_cd40 = 10, z_wtkg = 10, z_preanti = 10),
                 use_grf = FALSE, use_lasso = FALSE, maxk = 2,
                 hr.threshold = 0.90, hr.consistency = 0.80, pconsistency.threshold = 0.90,
                 sg_focus = "hrMaxSG", effect_neighborhood = 0.20),
  mr_inference_args = list(ci_method = "field", include_complement = TRUE, field_complement = TRUE,
                           draws = 2000, multiplier = "poisson", return_reselection = TRUE,
                           seed = seed_rep5))
one_call
# its H-hat, four sets and MR values equal the step-by-step objects above
num <- c("n", "n_exp", "n_ctl", "events_exp", "events_ctl", "hr", "lo", "hi")
mv_call <- mr_values(one_call$fs); mv_step <- mr_values(fs)
keep <- !grepl("timing", names(mv_step))
stopifnot(identical(one_call$Hhat, Hhat_def), identical(one_call$in_Hhat, in_Hhat),
          identical(one_call$sets$set, four$set),
          isTRUE(all.equal(one_call$sets[num], four[num], tolerance = 1e-12)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(mv_call[keep], mv_step[keep], tolerance = 1e-12)))
```

*With your trial:* your column names, your covariates in `fs_args$confounders.name` and your seed in
`mr_inference_args`, without `truth.name`. `$stage` says how far the pipeline went (`not_positive`,
`no_trigger`, `no_declaration` or `complete`), and none of these is an error; `plot()` on the result draws
the two figures of step 4, and `mr_values()` and `mr_estimates_table()` read its `$fs`.

The article took `r round((proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t_article) / 60, 1)` minutes to run.

# Appendix: the analysis window and the windowed Cox limit {#sec-window .unnumbered}

This appendix works through the callout "The windowed Cox limit" of @sec-dgm-overview for S2, on the
build of @sec-predictions (`dgm_pre`, whose hazard scale and regional shift are estimated from
replicate 5).

**What the multiplier changes.** `scale_dgm_hazard(dgm, m)` replaces the intercept $\mu$ by
$\mu - \tau\log m$, so $\Lambda_0(s) = (s\,e^{-\mu})^{1/\tau}$ becomes
$$
m\,\Lambda_0(s) = \Lambda_0(m^{\tau} s):
$$
every patient's hazard, on both arms, is multiplied by $m$, which is the same as running every
patient's clock $m^{\tau}$ times faster. No $\theta_z(X)$ changes, so no patient's hazard ratio
changes, and neither do three summaries of a set that depend on the $\theta$'s alone: the AHR, the
CDE, and margHR($\infty$) — a Cox fit with no censoring uses only the order of the event times, and
running every clock faster does not reorder them. What changes is how many events fall inside the
analysis window, whose limits are fixed in calendar months.

**A set's hazard ratio over follow-up.** At month $s$ of follow-up, a set's hazard ratio is each arm's
mean hazard among its patients still event-free, experimental over control. At $s = 0$ every patient
is at risk and it is the CDE; then it moves as patients have events (@fig-window, panel a). In S2 both
the trial's and the region's start above 1.0 and fall below it within the first year.

**What the Cox fit estimates.** margHR(40) is the constant hazard ratio that, applied to the patients
at risk at every event time, reproduces the experimental arm's share of the events inside the window:
in effect, an average of the set's curve over the window's events. In panel (a) the window is shaded
(every patient is followed to 29 months, the last enrolled to 40) and the dashed segments are the two
sets' margHR(40).

```{r window-limits}
#| code-fold: show
# dgm_pre runs on S2's clock (x 3, estimated from the trial): scaling it by M / 3 puts it at M x ACTG 175's hazards
M_grid <- 3^seq(-3, 4, by = 0.25)
clock <- do.call(rbind, lapply(M_grid, function(M) {
  pop_M <- ahr_population(scale_dgm_hazard(dgm_pre, M / 3), analysis_time = 40, max_entry = 11)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(c("all", "region"), function(s) {
    e <- ahr_limit(pop_M, s, b = 0.55, h = 2, variance = FALSE)
    data.frame(M = M, set = s, margHR40 = e$hr, AHR = e$ahr, CDE = e$cde,
               margHRinf = e$marghr_inf, events = e$d)
  }))
}))
ck <- function(s, M, v) clock[[v]][clock$set == s & abs(clock$M - M) < 1e-9]
# the region without its prognostic shift, at S2's rate: S2 with every hazard multiplied by exp(-r)
pop_nor <- ahr_population(scale_dgm_hazard(dgm_pre, exp(-r_pre)), analysis_time = 40, max_entry = 11)
reg_nor <- ahr_limit(pop_nor, "region", b = 0.55, h = 2, variance = FALSE)$hr
# a set's hazard ratio at month s: each arm's mean hazard among its event-free patients
hr_at <- function(dgm, in_set, months) {
  ds <- dgm$df_super[in_set, ]; mp <- dgm$model_params
  e0 <- exp(ds$theta_0); e1 <- exp(ds$theta_1)
  vapply(months, function(s) {
    u <- (s * exp(-mp$mu))^(1 / mp$tau)                  # Lambda_0(s), S2's clock
    (sum(e1 * exp(-u * e1)) / sum(exp(-u * e1))) / (sum(e0 * exp(-u * e0)) / sum(exp(-u * e0)))
  }, numeric(1))
}
months <- seq(0, 120, by = 0.5)
in_reg <- dgm_pre$df_super$z_region == 1
prof <- list(all = hr_at(dgm_pre, rep(TRUE, length(in_reg)), months), region = hr_at(dgm_pre, in_reg, months))
tau <- dgm_pre$model_params$tau
reach <- 40 * (c(1, 3, 9) / 3)^tau                         # where 40 months at x1, x3, x9 end on S2's clock
# the multiplier leaves each set's AHR, CDE and margHR(inf) unchanged; each curve starts at its CDE
for (s in c("all", "region")) for (v in c("AHR", "CDE", "margHRinf"))
  stopifnot(near(clock[[v]][clock$set == s], ck(s, 3, v), 1e-6))
stopifnot(near(c(prof$all[1], prof$region[1]), c(ck("all", 3, "CDE"), ck("region", 3, "CDE")), 1e-9))
# the verbal claims of this appendix and of the callout in the design section
stopifnot(all(vapply(prof, function(p) p[1] > 1 && min(p[months <= 12]) < 1, NA)),
          abs(ck("all", 1/27, "margHR40") / ck("all", 3, "CDE") - 1) < 0.02,
          abs(ck("all", 81, "margHR40") / ck("all", 3, "margHRinf") - 1) < 0.002,
          abs(log(ck("all", 3, "AHR") / c(ck("all", 3, "CDE"), ck("all", 3, "margHRinf")))) > 0.01,
          ck("region", 3, "margHR40") / ck("region", 3, "CDE") > ck("all", 3, "margHR40") / ck("all", 3, "CDE"),
          ck("region", 3, "margHR40") > ck("all", 3, "margHR40"), reg_nor < ck("all", 3, "margHR40"),
          round(5 * ck("all", 1, "events")) == 1)
```

```{r fig-window}

(a) Each set's hazard ratio at each month of follow-up on S2's clock (each arm's mean hazard among the set's event-free patients); shaded, the 40-month analysis window; dashed, each set's margHR(40); bars, how far 40 months reach on this clock at 1, 3 and 9 times ACTG 175's hazards. (b) margHR(40) against the hazard multiplier, with each set's CDE (dashed) and margHR(∞) (dotted); the right-hand ticks are the AHRs."
col_set <- c(all = "#1f3b73", region = "#c4661f")
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4.2, 4.2, 2.6, 5.4), mgp = c(2.4, 0.7, 0), las = 1)

}
y_bar <- c(1.28, 1.21, 1.14)
segments(0, y_bar, reach, y_bar, lwd = 2.5, col = "grey25")
text(reach, y_bar, c("x1 (ACTG 175)", "x3 (S2)", "x9"), pos = 4, cex = 0.8)
legend("bottomright", c("all patients", "region"), col = col_set, lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.85)
box()
# (b) margHR(40) against the hazard multiplier
plot(NA, xlim = range(clock$M), ylim = c(0.55, 1.32), log = "xy", xaxt = "n",
     xlab = "hazard multiplier (x ACTG 175's hazards)", ylab = "hazard ratio",
     main = "(b) margHR(40) as the multiplier changes", font.main = 1)
axis(1, at = 3^(-3:4), labels = c("1/27", "1/9", "1/3", "1", "3", "9", "27", "81"))
abline(v = c(1, 3, 9), col = "grey80"); abline(h = 1, col = "grey50", lty = 3)
for (s in c("all", "region")) {
  d <- clock[clock$set == s, ]
  abline(h = d$CDE[1], col = col_set[[s]], lty = 2)
  abline(h = d$margHRinf[1], col = col_set[[s]], lty = 3, lwd = 1.5)
  axis(4, at = d$AHR[1], labels = FALSE, col.ticks = col_set[[s]], lwd.ticks = 2, tcl = 1.2)
  lines(d$M, d$margHR40, col = col_set[[s]], lwd = 2)
  keep <- d$M %in% c(1, 3, 9)

}
mtext(c("CDE", expression("margHR(" * infinity * ")"), "AHR"), side = 4, line = 0.5, las = 1,
      cex = 0.75,

```

**The window sits later on the faster clock.** By $m\,\Lambda_0(s) = \Lambda_0(m^{\tau} s)$, a trial at
$m$ times the hazards, analysed at 40 months, sees what the unscaled trial sees at $40\,m^{\tau}$
months, with its entry period stretched alike: the curves stay where they are, and the fixed 40-month
window covers more of them. With $\hat\tau$ = `r f3(tau)`, 40 months at ACTG 175's rate (×1) cover
the first `r round(reach[1])` months of S2's clock, and at ×9 the first `r round(reach[3])` (the bars
in panel a). Panel (b) follows margHR(40) across multipliers. As $m \to 0$ the few events come before
anyone has left, and the limit tends to the CDE; as $m \to \infty$ every event falls inside the window,
and it tends to margHR($\infty$). In between it moves although no patient's hazard ratio has: for all
patients from `r f3(ck("all", 1, "margHR40"))` at ×1 to `r f3(ck("all", 3, "margHR40"))` at S2's ×3,
and for the region from `r f3(ck("region", 1, "margHR40"))` to `r f3(ck("region", 3, "margHR40"))`,
while the share of patients with an event in the window goes from `r pc(ck("all", 1, "events"))`% to
`r pc(ck("all", 3, "events"))`%. Neither end is the AHR (`r f3(ck("all", 3, "AHR"))` for all
patients).

**The region runs on a slower clock.** The shift $r$ multiplies the region's hazards by $e^{r}$ on
both arms, so it acts on the region exactly as a multiplier acts on the trial: the region with its
shift, at multiplier $m$, is the region without it at $m\,e^{r}$. Here $e^{\hat r}$ =
`r f3(exp(r_pre))` slows the region's clock: its curve in panel (a) runs later, and its 40-month
window ends earlier on it, nearer the CDE. Removing the shift — for the region's own limit, the same
as multiplying every hazard by $e^{-\hat r}$, one more `scale_dgm_hazard()` call — moves the region's
margHR(40) at S2's rate from `r f3(ck("region", 3, "margHR40"))` to `r f3(reg_nor)`, below the trial's
`r f3(ck("all", 3, "margHR40"))`.

**What follows.**

- The multiplier sets the event rate and nothing else: $b$, $h$, and every set's AHR, CDE and
  margHR($\infty$) are as set at every multiplier.
- The pipeline's Cox fits estimate their sets' margHR(40), so where the trial's estimates fall — and
  with them the probabilities of @sec-predictions — depends on the event rate and the window as well
  as on the effects. A regional estimate near or above 1.0 can come from a trial-wide harmed subgroup
  in a region of lower baseline risk, with no regional difference in treatment effect: the region's
  window holds the early part of its curve, where the harmed patients' events weigh most.
- In a real trial nothing is multiplied: the trial's own event rate and follow-up set the clock. The
  same set can give a different Cox estimate at a later analysis with no patient's effect changed, and
  a region of lower baseline risk is seen earlier on its curve than the rest of the trial at the same
  analysis time.

# Appendix: the manuscript's event notation {#sec-event-notation .unnumbered}

The accompanying manuscript collects the design's events in its Table 1, reproduced here; a
superscript $+$ ($-$) marks a point estimate or bound in (opposite to) the direction of consistency.
This article's $A$, $B$ and $C^*$ are $\mathrm{ITT}^+$, $\mathrm{R}^-$ and $\mathrm{R}(G^*)^+$.

| Event | Definition | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| *Primitive events* | | |
| $\mathrm{ITT}^+$ | {ITT 95% upper bound < 1.0} | The trial is positive |
| $\mathrm{R}^-$, $\mathrm{R}^+$ | {region ITT > 1.0}, {region ITT $\le$ 1.0} | Region point estimate opposite to, in, the direction of consistency |
| $\mathrm{R}(G^*)^-$, $\mathrm{R}(G^*)^+$ | {region($G^*$) > 1.0}, {region($G^*$) $\le$ 1.0} | Likewise, for the region outside the true subgroup $H^*$ |
| $\mathrm{R}(\hat G)^+$ | {subgroup declared, region($\hat G$) < 1.0} | The declared resolution is in the consistent direction |
| *Named events* | | |
| consistency | $\mathrm{ITT}^+ \cap \mathrm{R}^+$ | Positive trial, region in the consistent direction — the standard pathway |
| non-consistency | $\mathrm{ITT}^+ \cap \mathrm{R}^-$ | Positive trial, region opposite — the trigger for subgroup identification |
| oracle consistency | $\mathrm{ITT}^+ \cap \mathrm{R}^- \cap \mathrm{R}(G^*)^+$ | Non-consistency resolved by the true subgroup |
| oracle non-consistency | $\mathrm{ITT}^+ \cap \mathrm{R}^- \cap \mathrm{R}(G^*)^-$ | Non-consistency persisting under the oracle resolution |
| declared consistency | $\mathrm{ITT}^+ \cap \mathrm{R}^- \cap \mathrm{R}(\hat G)^+$ | Non-consistency resolved by the declared subgroup |

: The manuscript's Table 1: event notation.
